dedupe_keys.name: opentrafficsim ots open source multi level multimodal traffic simulator tu delft

description: OpenTrafficSim (OTS) is an open-source Java traffic simulation environment that aims to combine micro-, macro- and meta-simulation and all traffic modes, from private cars and buses to bicycles and pedestrians, in one simulator, with options to link external code, driving simulators and data sources. It is developed by researchers at Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands. Coverage: a generic tool, not a regional model; the manual describes link- and lane-level networks, demand from origin-destination matrices and generators, driver perception and mental models, strategic and tactical planners and lane-change models, conflict areas and queue spillback. Format and access: Java source on GitHub built on the DSOL discrete-event simulation library, with a technical manual, tutorials and Javadoc APIs on opentrafficsim.org; outputs include trajectory, detector and performance indicator data, and a co-simulation protocol links it to external programs; free. Licence: BSD 3-Clause, copyright 2014-2026 Delft University of Technology. Caveats: road traffic is the most developed part (the documented API modules are ots-base, ots-core and ots-road), the multimodal aims are partly aspirational, and users need Java development skills. Simulation uses: microscopic studies of road capacity, lane-level behaviour, incident spillback and co-simulated driving experiments for network flow and capacity planning. Related records: Eclipse SUMO (model-sumo) and PTV Vissim (model-ptv-vissim) are the main open and commercial microscopic alternatives.
